lines.text: call comes no excuse can be admitted, and it cannot be
overlooked. Then the question for us is whether it is the call
of God who summons us thus into His presence, or whether
it is the sinister call of fate plunging us into nothingness.
Then the decisive issue for us will be whether we are ready
and whether in the course of our earthly life we have learnt
to be ready for the challenges of God.
We have not spoken specifically about the fate which at
the present time has overtaken us, and the terrifying and
tragic nature, of which we are painfully conscious, of this
very day. Is it necessary to speak of it specially now?
Whoever has understood all that is implied in the demands
of Christian vigilance and preparedness, about which our
parable warns us, will also realize what these demands
imply just now above all. No doubt even without meditation
on this parable we shall all know that we must hold our-
selves ready to meet whatever the future may bring by our
readiness for action and self-sacrifice, and by calm bravery.
Beyond all this, however, our parable warns us to be pre-
pared for what God wishes to say to us in the events which
loom ahead. It teaches us to seek the firm ground on which
alone we can find genuine peace and the inspiration for
courage, on which we can win an inner detachment from
everything that our earthly future may bring of good and ill,
victories and sacrifices-that inner detachment which we
win when we are ready for God's future, and cling to Him
in calm trust.
